record.narrative: Initial round tests biologically grounded predictor-outcome pairs in the supplied lung-cell-line dataset. Dependency scores are continuous with more negative values indicating stronger dependency; therefore a direction of -1 encodes the expected exposure-minus-comparator mean difference being negative, i.e. stronger dependency in the exposed group. For direct target dependencies, the expected effects are stronger dependency in cells harboring activating mutations or amplifications of the same gene: KRAS mutation for dependency_KRAS, BRAF V600E for dependency_BRAF, EGFR amplification for dependency_EGFR, and ERBB2 amplification for dependency_ERBB2. Alternative explanations include that mutation status may be a marker of pathway context rather than a direct causal modifier, or that co-occurring oncogenic lesions could dilute the apparent single-gene association. For p53 pathway dependencies, TP53 wild-type cells are expected to have stronger MDM2 and USP7 dependency than TP53-loss cells because MDM2 and USP7 regulate p53 protein turnover and activity; TP53-loss cells may be less reliant on the p53-MDM2 axis. Alternatives include p53-independent essential functions of MDM2/USP7 and confounding by other genetic events. For chromatin dependencies, SMARCA4 or ARID1A loss is expected to create stronger SMARCA2 dependency through SWI/SNF paralog buffering or synthetic lethality; alternatives are that different SWI/SNF losses have distinct effects or that SMARCA2 dependency is dominated by lineage or chromatin state. WRN dependency is expected to be stronger in MSI-high cells, a context where WRN loss is often selectively detrimental; alternatives are that the MSI signal could be confounded by mutation burden or microsatellite-associated transcriptomic programs. KEAP1 loss is expected to be associated with stronger NFE2L2 dependency because KEAP1 loss activates NRF2 pathway programs and may increase pathway reliance; alternatives are pathway saturation or that KEAP1 loss reduces NFE2L2 essentiality if antioxidant stress tolerance is already maximally engaged. PIK3CA mutation is proposed as an exploratory predictor of STAT3 dependency through PI3K/AKT-associated survival signaling, with substantial uncertainty. MYC amplification is proposed as a predictor of stronger POLR2A dependency because MYC-amplified cells may be more transcription-addicted. All claims are registered as unresolved; we will judge acceptance only after seeing Welch intervals and whether the signed effects are both statistically reliable and of magnitude consistent with the stated ~10% relative clinical-significance benchmark for these dependency scores.

No evidence is yet available, so I am requesting analyses for all twelve registered round-1 comparisons. These cover the highest-prior mechanistic tests: direct oncogene alteration/target dependency associations for KRAS, BRAF, EGFR, and ERBB2; p53-pathway context for MDM2 and USP7; SWI/SNF buffering for SMARCA2; MSI-associated WRN dependency; KEAP1-loss-associated NFE2L2 dependency; and exploratory pathway associations for PIK3CA-STAT3 and MYC-POLR2A. All have enough cells under the >=20-per-cell requirement based on variable frequencies. After results arrive, I will judge whether each signed estimate is statistically supported by its 95% Welch interval and whether its magnitude is scientifically/clinically meaningful relative to the dependency scale and the stated 10% relative-difference benchmark.

All estimates are already signed to the registered claim direction. For the direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast was negative, i.e. stronger dependency in the exposed group; a negative signed estimate means the opposite. Four comparisons give unambiguous evidence after 12-test multiplicity: H6, H7, H9, and H10. H6: TP53 wild-type cells have much stronger USP7 dependency than TP53-loss cells; the signed interval is entirely positive and the effect is far larger than any plausible 10% relative benchmark. H7: SMARCA4-loss cells have much stronger SMARCA2 dependency than SMARCA4-intact cells; the signed interval is entirely positive and very large. H9: MSI-high cells have much stronger WRN dependency than MSI-low cells; the signed interval is entirely positive and very large. H10 shows a large effect, but the signed interval is entirely negative under a direction -1 claim, meaning KEAP1-loss cells have weaker NFE2L2 dependency/higher dependency score rather than stronger dependency. Therefore H10 is rejected as originally formulated, and I propose a reversed claim. The remaining direct-target and exploratory associations are not supported: H1 KRAS mutation vs KRAS dependency is small and crosses zero; H2 BRAF V600E and H4 ERBB2 amplification are small and opposite/null; H5 TP53 status vs MDM2 dependency is tiny; H8 ARID1A loss vs SMARCA2 dependency is null; H11 PIK3CA vs STAT3 and H12 MYC amplification vs POLR2A are null. H3 EGFR amplification vs EGFR dependency is borderline: the signed point estimate is about 0.025, possibly near a 10% relative scale, but the 95% interval includes zero and could be diluted by co-occurring oncogenic lesions, so I leave it unresolved and propose testing EGFR-amplified KRAS-wild-type cells. I request independent validation for H7 because the SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 effect is very large, biologically plausible, and potentially actionable, while also checking whether this is not a one-sample artifact. These conclusions are associations in this dataset only and do not establish causality or generalizability.

The newly released validation for H7 strongly corroborates the original SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 association. The validation estimate is already signed to the claim direction and is +0.805, with an independent 95% interval +0.774 to +0.835. Because the interval excludes zero by a very wide margin and the effect is far larger than the stated 10% relative benchmark, the original claim is not a discovery-set-only borderline signal: in this dataset, SMARCA4-loss cells have substantially stronger SMARCA2 dependency than SMARCA4-intact cells. I therefore accept H7 and close the original claim as established in this dataset, while keeping the separate ARID1A-interaction refinements active to test whether the association is uniform across SWI/SNF co-alteration contexts.

I also reassess H13, the reversed form of the original KEAP1/NFE2L2 claim. The reversed-direction estimate is +0.796, with interval +0.776 to +0.816, and the outcome is a CRISPR dependency score where more negative values indicate stronger dependency. Thus KEAP1-loss cells have a higher, less negative dependency_NFE2L2 score: they are not more dependent on NFE2L2; if anything, they appear less dependent on NFE2L2. This is a large, statistically unambiguous association in the supplied dataset and is accepted as H13. It does not by itself prove that KEAP1 loss reduces NFE2L2 essentiality; it may be mediated by co-occurring alterations such as STK11 or TP53 events, or by pathway-state differences. I therefore keep H13 active and propose conditional/robustness checks.

At present, the strongest accepted dataset associations are: TP53 wild-type cells have stronger USP7 dependency than TP53-loss cells; SMARCA4-loss cells have stronger SMARCA2 dependency than SMARCA4-intact cells; MSI-high cells have stronger WRN dependency than MSI-low cells; and KEAP1-loss cells have weaker NFE2L2 dependency/higher dependency scores. All accepted effects are extremely large on the dependency-score scale, several standard deviations, and are well beyond the 10% relative-difference threshold. The original H10 formulation is rejected because it was directionally wrong for KEAP1/NFE2L2.

The negative or null findings remain closed: KRAS mutation, BRAF V600E, and ERBB2 amplification did not show reliable same-target dependency differences; TP53 status did not reliably predict MDM2 dependency; ARID1A loss alone did not reliably predict SMARCA2 dependency; and PIK3CA mutation and MYC amplification did not reliably predict STAT3 or POLR2A dependency in this dataset. EGFR amplification remains unresolved because the discovery effect is borderline and the interval includes zero; I have proposed KRAS-wild-type and alternate-library follow-ups to determine whether co-occurring MAPK-pathway alterations or technical/library context dilute a possible effect.

The next most informative analyses are the already registered refinements: whether the SMARCA4-loss effect depends on ARID1A loss, whether the WRN MSI association persists when restricting to higher mutation burden, whether the USP7 TP53 wild-type effect persists in MYC-amplified cells, and whether EGFR amplification becomes clearer in KRAS-wild-type cells. I additionally propose alternate-library checks in the KY library for the top accepted effects and the EGFR signal, plus a TP53-loss interaction for KEAP1/NFE2L2. These will distinguish robust biological subgroup effects from potential screen/library or co-alteration confounding. All conclusions remain associations within the supplied lung-cell-line dataset; causal direction, clinical relevance, and generalizability remain unestablished.

The main accepted signals are now established in this dataset at a discovery level: TP53 wild-type cells are far more dependent on USP7; SMARCA4-loss cells are far more dependent on SMARCA2; MSI-high cells are far more dependent on WRN; and KEAP1-loss cells have weaker NFE2L2 dependency/higher dependency scores. The next step should combine robustness checking with broadening to untested dependency outcomes. I register several new hypotheses in the same sign convention: direction -1 means the exposed group is expected to have a more negative dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency; direction +1 means the exposed group is expected to have a less negative score, i.e. weaker dependency. For DHX9, MSI-high status is expected to increase reliance on DNA repair/replication-stress responses, so msi_high is tested with direction -1. For KIF18A, TP53-loss or genomic-instability contexts may increase dependence on chromosome-segregation machinery, so tp53_loss is tested with direction -1, while alternatives include no effect because KIF18A essentiality could be proliferation-driven rather than TP53-state-specific. For RPL11, MYC amplification is hypothesized to increase ribosome/translation addiction, so myc_amplification is tested with direction -1. For TMED10, EGFR-amplified cells may have increased secretory or receptor-trafficking demand, so egfr_amplification is tested with direction -1. For MDM2, the prior overall TP53-loss comparison was null, but MYC amplification within TP53-wild-type cells may increase MDM2 dependence because MYC-induced ARF/p53 stress could make cells more reliant on MDM2-mediated p53 suppression; therefore I test myc_amplification within TP53_loss=0 with direction -1. To interrogate the reversed KEAP1/NFE2L2 finding, I test whether the high NFE2L2 score in KEAP1-loss cells persists among STK11-wild-type cells; if STK11 co-alteration is a major confounder, the STK11=0 estimate could attenuate, whereas a persistent estimate would strengthen the dataset-level claim. Finally, I request adenocarcinoma-restricted checks for the USP7/TP53 and WRN/MSI effects to assess within-dataset subtype robustness. These remain associations in the supplied lung-cell-line resource and are not yet claims about causality, clinical biomarkers, or external generalizability.

I will request twelve analyses focused first on the strongest current dataset-level signals and their plausible confounders, before moving broadly into low-prior new predictor-outcome pairs. For H7, which is already accepted and independently validated, I request H14, H15, and H16 to test whether the SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 dependency association is modified by ARID1A loss. H14 and H15 estimate the effect within ARID1A-loss and ARID1A-intact contexts, while H16 directly tests the corresponding interaction; together these distinguish a broadly robust SWI/SNF buffering effect from an association concentrated in a co-alteration subgroup.

For the accepted WRN/MSI-high signal, I request H17 and H33 rather than the KY-library WRN check because the MSI-high cell count is small and could fail the 20-per-cell requirement within the KY library. H17 asks whether the MSI-high effect persists after restricting to higher mutation burden, addressing whether MSI-high is merely a proxy for high tumor mutational burden. H33 asks whether the association remains in the larger adenocarcinoma subset, providing a within-dataset subtype robustness check.

For the accepted USP7/TP53 signal, I request H18, H21, and H23: H18 tests the effect within MYC-amplified cells, H21 tests it within the KY CRISPR library, and H23 provides an additional library-context check for the SMARCA2 effect. These address whether the large TP53-dependent USP7 association is context-dependent or an artifact of particular co-alteration or screen-library distributions.

For the accepted but directionally surprising KEAP1/NFE2L2 result, I request H25 and H31. H31 tests whether the high NFE2L2 dependency score in KEAP1-loss cells persists among STK11-wild-type cells, which helps assess whether STK11 co-alteration confounds the association. H25 tests a KEAP1-by-TP53-loss interaction to determine whether the effect is uniform across p53 status. I also retain H22 as a KY-library check for KEAP1/NFE2L2.

Finally, H19 follows up the unresolved EGFR result by testing EGFR amplification only in KRAS-wild-type cells, where a direct EGFR-dependency association is less likely to be diluted by mutually exclusive or co-occurring MAPK-pathway alterations. I omit H20 and H24 from this batch because the relevant exposure cells could be sparse within the KY library, and I defer several new outcome screens until the current robustness checks are interpreted. All requested directions follow the sign convention: direction -1 encodes a more negative dependency score in the exposed group, meaning stronger dependency; direction +1 encodes a less negative score, meaning weaker dependency.

The new robustness analyses substantially strengthen the accepted main associations, while the EGFR and interaction follow-ups remain unsupported or null. All reported estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. For direction -1, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has a more negative dependency score, i.e. stronger CRISPR dependency. For direction +1, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has a less negative dependency score, i.e. weaker dependency.  SMARCA4 loss/SMARCA2: H14 estimates the SMARCA4-loss effect within ARID1A-loss cells at +0.814 with interval +0.767 to +0.862; H15 estimates the effect within ARID1A-intact cells at +0.777 with interval +0.756 to +0.798. Both are far from zero, with very large magnitude on the dependency-score scale, and both intervals exclude zero by margins far larger than multiple-comparison-adjusted thresholds. H16 estimates an ARID1A modification interaction of +0.037 with interval -0.015 to +0.089; the interval crosses zero and the point estimate is small. Thus the SMARCA4-loss association appears present in both ARID1A-loss and ARID1A-intact contexts, but there is no reliable evidence that ARID1A loss modifies it.  WRN/MSI: H17 estimates the MSI-high WRN effect after restricting to cells with mutation burden >=4 as +0.787, interval +0.757 to +0.817. Because the exposed MSI-high cell count is the same as in the original analysis, this mainly shows that the comparator was not low-mutation-burden cells rather than proving a true MSI-specific interaction, but it still weakens the simple explanation that the association arises because MSI-high cells are compared with generally genomically quiet cells. H33 estimates the MSI-high WRN effect within adenocarcinoma as +0.784, interval +0.748 to +0.820. These are dataset robustness checks, not independent validation.  USP7/TP53: H18 estimates the TP53-wild-type USP7 dependency effect within MYC-amplified cells as +0.803, interval +0.754 to +0.852. H21 estimates it within the KY library as +0.773, interval +0.733 to +0.812. The USP7 association is therefore not explained by MYC amplification alone or by the KY library subset.  EGFR amplification: H19 tests EGFR-amplified KRAS-wild-type cells and yields +0.016, interval -0.014 to +0.046. The point estimate is small and the interval includes zero. This does not support a direct EGFR amplification/EGFR dependency association in this dataset and argues against simple dilution by KRAS mutation as the sole explanation for the borderline H3 signal. I therefore reject H19 as an evidenced association, while leaving the original H3 claim unresolved pending remaining technical checks.  KEAP1/NFE2L2: H22 estimates the reversed KEAP1-loss effect within the KY library as +0.794, interval +0.752 to +0.837. H31 estimates the effect among STK11-wild-type cells as +0.801, interval +0.779 to +0.823. H25 estimates a KEAP1-by-TP53-loss interaction as +0.018, interval -0.034 to +0.069, which is small and crosses zero. Thus the large dataset-level observation that KEAP1-loss cells have weaker NFE2L2 dependency/higher dependency scores is robust across library and STK11 context, with no evidence of modification by TP53 loss. Because H13 is a large, biologically counterintuitive reversed claim, I request independent validation of H13; the robustness checks are reassuring but not an independent replication.  Overall, the strongest supported dataset-level associations remain: TP53-wild-type cells have stronger USP7 dependency; SMARCA4-loss cells have stronger SMARCA2 dependency; MSI-high cells have stronger WRN dependency; and KEAP1-loss cells have weaker NFE2L2 dependency/higher dependency scores. These are associations within the supplied lung-cell-line dataset, not causal effects, clinical biomarkers, or externally generalizable claims.

No new validation was released for this synthesis; the only independent validation available remains the validation of H7. Therefore, the currently strongest evidence in the supplied lung-cell-line dataset consists of four very large dataset-level associations, each far exceeding any plausible 10% relative-difference benchmark on the dependency-score scale. Because many dependency scores have negative means, I judged the clinical-significance threshold primarily against the scale and standard deviation of the dependency scores rather than as a literal percent change in a negative quantity; all accepted effects are around 0.75 to 0.85, i.e. several standard deviations.

The accepted associations are: H6, TP53-wild-type cells have much stronger USP7 dependency than TP53-loss cells; H7, SMARCA4-loss cells have much stronger SMARCA2 dependency than SMARCA4-intact cells, and this claim is independently validated by R13; H9, MSI-high cells have much stronger WRN dependency than MSI-low cells; and H13, KEAP1-loss cells have weaker NFE2L2 dependency, i.e. a less negative/higher dependency_NFE2L2 score, than KEAP1-intact cells. H13 is the reversed, biologically counterintuitive version of the original H10 formulation, and H10 was correctly rejected as directionally wrong.

The robustness follow-ups materially strengthen the accepted effects but do not establish causality or external generalizability. The SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 association is present both when ARID1A is lost and when it is intact, with estimates +0.814 and +0.777, respectively, and the ARID1A-by-SMARCA4 interaction is small and crosses zero, so there is no reliable evidence that ARID1A loss modifies the main association. The SMARCA4 effect is also retained in the KY-library subset. The USP7/TP53 wild-type association is retained within MYC-amplified cells and within the KY-library subset. The WRN/MSI-high association is retained in adenocarcinoma and after restricting the comparator to cells with mutation burden of at least four, although H17 is not a true interaction test because the exposed MSI-high set is largely unchanged. The KEAP1/NFE2L2 association is retained in the KY-library subset and among STK11-wild-type cells, and the KEAP1-by-TP53-loss interaction is small and crosses zero. Thus, within this dataset, the four accepted associations are robust to the measured contexts tested so far.

The negative and null findings are also now more interpretable. Same-target associations were not supported for KRAS mutation versus KRAS dependency, BRAF V600E versus BRAF dependency, ERBB2 amplification versus ERBB2 dependency, PIK3CA mutation versus STAT3 dependency, or MYC amplification versus POLR2A dependency. Overall TP53 status did not predict MDM2 dependency. ARID1A loss alone did not predict SMARCA2 dependency. The KRAS-wild-type EGFR follow-up was small and compatible with no effect, although the original overall EGFR amplification claim remains unresolved because the initial estimate was borderline and its interval included zero. No reliable interaction evidence was found for ARID1A modifying the SMARCA4-loss effect or TP53-loss modifying the KEAP1/NFE2L2 effect.

The next most informative step is to test the unresolved claims and broaden coverage of the untested dependency outcomes. I request that the next appraise cycle prioritize independent validation of H13, because it is large but directionally unexpected and therefore has the highest value from an independent replication. If H13 validates well, H9 and H6 would also be strong validation candidates. The discovery queue should include H26 through H32 and H34 through H39, plus the newly registered RIT1/KRAS redundancy hypothesis: KRAS mutation may make RIT1 less essential because KRAS-mutant cells have constitutive MAPK-pathway activation, so direction +1 encodes a weaker RIT1 dependency/higher score. Direct-target refinements for BRAF, EGFR, or ERBB2 in mutually exclusive oncogenic contexts may be useful later, but the current priority is to fill untested outcomes and obtain validation for the main accepted effects. All conclusions remain associations within the supplied lung-cell-line dataset; causal direction, clinical biomarker status, and generalizability remain unestablished.

The accepted dataset-level associations are now strong enough to justify shifting from broad confirmation toward targeted mechanistic robustness and coverage of the remaining untested dependency outcomes. The four largest accepted effects are TP53 wild-type stronger USP7 dependency, SMARCA4 loss stronger SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high stronger WRN dependency, and KEAP1 loss weaker NFE2L2 dependency/higher dependency score. These remain associations within the supplied lung cell-line dataset, not causal claims or clinically validated biomarkers. I registered refinements that can either strengthen these effects in biologically distinct contexts or reveal whether they are confined to particular co-alteration states: NFE2L2/KEAP1 in adenocarcinoma, WRN/MSI among TP53 wild-type cells, USP7 by ARID1A-loss context, and SMARCA2 by TP53-loss context. For WRN, I used a mean difference among TP53 wild-type cells rather than a full MSI-by-TP53 interaction because the MSI-high by TP53-loss exposed cell may be near the minimum cell-count requirement. For USP7 and SMARCA2, interaction tests are more likely to have adequate cells and directly test modification.

The EGFR and ERBB2 claims need better conditional framing. The overall EGFR amplification result was borderline and positive-signed, whereas the KRAS wild-type restriction was small and nonsignificant. I registered a KRAS-wild-type and BRAF-wild-type EGFR check to test whether removing MAPK-pathway co-alterations unmasks a direct EGFR amplification effect. If this remains null, the EGFR amplification claim should probably be closed as unsupported in this dataset. For ERBB2, the overall association was very close to null; the KRAS/BRAF wild-type refinement tests whether a small effect was diluted by co-occurring pathway alterations. I also added a cross-target hypothesis that EGFR amplification in KRAS wild-type cells may increase dependency on KRAS itself because upstream receptor tyrosine kinase signaling can require wild-type RAS transmission.

For previously untested or weakly tested outcomes, I registered DHX9 versus TP53 loss, KIF18A versus MSI-high, and RIT1 versus KRAS mutation among BRAF wild-type cells. The DHX9 hypothesis is that TP53 loss increases replication stress and reliance on RNA/DNA helicase machinery. KIF18A is less predictable because MSI status and chromosome segregation defects are not guaranteed to move together, so I registered it as an uncertain but scientifically relevant check. For RIT1, KRAS mutation may reduce RIT1 essentiality by constitutively activating downstream MAPK signaling; restricting to BRAF wild-type cells reduces confounding from alternative MAPK activation. To improve the MYC-related translation hypotheses, I refined RPL11 and POLR2A by requiring both MYC amplification and relatively high MYC RNA expression at or above 5.0 log2 TPM. This addresses the possibility that MYC amplification alone was null because some amplified lines do not have corresponding MYC-pathway activity. TMED10 was tested with ERBB2 amplification because ERBB2-family receptor trafficking and secretory demand are conceptually parallel to the EGFR-secretory hypothesis, while avoiding another redundant EGFR follow-up.

I deferred several active lower-priority claims to make room for these higher-information refinements: EGFR in KY library and EGFR in BRAF wild-type are superseded by the KRAS/BRAF wild-type check; NFE2L2 by TP53-loss strata is partially superseded by the already null KEAP1-by-TP53 interaction and the new adenocarcinoma check; lineage subtype interactions for SMARCA2 and USP7 are deferred because the already robust subgroup/interaction checks are more directly interpretable; KIF18A/TP53 loss is deferred in favor of the new DHX9/TP53 and KIF18A/MSI checks; TMED10/EGFR is deferred in favor of TMED10/ERBB2; and overall RIT1/KRAS is deferred in favor of the BRAF wild-type refinement. Although validation cannot be requested at the explore stage, the next appraise should prioritize independent validation of H13 because it is large but directionally unexpected. H9 and H6 would be strong subsequent validation candidates if resources remain.

I will request twelve discovery tests chosen to make the current interpretation more decisive while still broadening coverage. First, I test context robustness for the accepted main effects: H41 asks whether KEAP1-loss cells retain weaker NFE2L2 dependency/higher NFE2L2 score in the larger adenocarcinoma subset; H42 asks whether MSI-high cells retain stronger WRN dependency among TP53-wild-type cells; H43 tests whether the TP53-wild-type USP7 effect is modified by ARID1A loss; and H44 tests whether the SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 effect is modified by TP53 loss. These address whether the four accepted effects are broad within measured biological states or confined to a co-alteration context. Second, I address the unresolved EGFR and ERBB2 direct-target questions. H45 removes both KRAS mutation and BRAF V600E from EGFR-amplified comparisons; if this remains small and null, the original EGFR amplification claim can be treated as unsupported in this dataset. H46 is the parallel ERBB2 conditional check, and H47 tests the biologically plausible cross-target possibility that EGFR amplification in RAS/RAF wild-type cells may increase dependence on wild-type KRAS. Third, I begin untested dependency outcomes and refinements: H48 tests DHX9 with TP53 loss, H49 tests KIF18A with MSI-high status, H50 tests whether KRAS mutation is associated with weaker RIT1 dependency in BRAF-wild-type cells, H51 tests MYC amplification with relatively high MYC expression on RPL11 dependency, and H53 tests ERBB2 amplification on TMED10 dependency. I omit H52, the analogous POLR2A high-MYC refinement, because overall MYC/POLR2A was already null and this batch prioritizes outcome diversity and unresolved direct-target checks. All requested directions follow the ledger sign convention: direction -1 encodes stronger dependency/more negative score in the exposed group, and direction +1 encodes weaker dependency/less negative or higher score in the exposed group.

All estimates are interpreted as already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. For direction -1, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has a more negative dependency score, i.e. stronger CRISPR dependency; for direction +1, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has a less negative/higher dependency score, i.e. weaker dependency. H41 accepts the KEAP1-loss/weak-NFE2L2 pattern within adenocarcinoma: the signed estimate is +0.793 with interval +0.769 to +0.817. This is several standard deviations on the dependency-score scale and is far larger than the small null associations seen for direct receptor-tyrosine-kinase target hypotheses. H42 accepts the MSI-high/strong-WRN association among TP53-wild-type cells: signed estimate +0.780, interval +0.747 to +0.813. Thus the WRN effect is not confined to TP53-loss backgrounds. H43 and H44 test modification of the accepted USP7 and SMARCA2 effects by ARID1A loss and TP53 loss. Their interaction estimates are small and cross zero: H43 -0.016 with interval -0.066 to +0.034, and H44 -0.015 with interval -0.064 to +0.035. I therefore reject these interaction claims as unsupported, while preserving the already accepted main effects and their prior robustness checks. H45 rejects the EGFR-amplification/EGFR-dependency hypothesis after removing KRAS and BRAF co-alterations: signed estimate +0.010, interval -0.020 to +0.041. H46 rejects the parallel ERBB2 conditional claim: signed estimate -0.011, interval -0.047 to +0.024. H47 rejects the cross-target hypothesis that EGFR amplification in RAS/RAF wild-type cells increases dependence on KRAS: signed estimate -0.0005, interval -0.033 to +0.032. H48 is rejected even though the 95% interval narrowly excludes zero, because the signed estimate is -0.020 for a direction -1 claim, meaning the observed association is weakly opposite to the hypothesis: TP53 loss is associated with a higher/less negative DHX9 score, i.e. weaker dependency. The magnitude is tiny relative to the outcome standard deviation and only marginal in a multiplicity-rich discovery setting, so I do not accept the original directional claim or its reversal as scientifically meaningful. H49, H50, H51, and H53 are all close to null: KIF18A/MSI-high, RIT1/KRAS in BRAF-wild-type cells, RPL11/MYC amplification within high MYC expression, and TMED10/ERBB2 amplification show intervals crossing zero with very small point estimates. I also reassess the original EGFR claim H3 using the overall borderline result plus the KRAS-wild-type and KRAS/BRAF-wild-type conditional null checks. Given that the overall estimate is small, its interval includes zero, and the mechanistically motivated conditional analyses are also null, H3 is rejected and closed as an unsupported dataset association. The strongest currently supported associations remain the very large TP53-wild-type/USP7, SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2, MSI-high/WRN, and KEAP1-loss/weak-NFE2L2 effects, plus the robustness checks in adenocarcinoma and TP53-wild-type subsets for the NFE2L2 and WRN claims. Because H13 is large but directionally counterintuitive, I request independent validation for H13. These remain associations within the supplied dataset, not causal effects or externally generalizable clinical claims.

The new validation results materially strengthen the leading claims. All estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction: for direction -1, a positive estimate means stronger dependency/more negative score in the exposed group; for direction +1, a positive estimate means weaker dependency/less negative score in the exposed group.

H7 is independently validated. The discovery result for SMARCA4-loss cells having stronger SMARCA2 dependency was +0.784 with a 95% discovery interval +0.765 to +0.803; validation gave +0.805 with an independent interval +0.774 to +0.836. The two estimates are nearly identical and both are extremely large relative to the SMARCA2 dependency-score scale. I therefore keep H7 accepted and close its investigation.

H13 is now independently validated. This is the reversed, biologically counterintuitive claim that KEAP1-loss cells have weaker NFE2L2 dependency, i.e. a higher/less negative dependency_NFE2L2 score. Discovery was +0.796; validation was +0.802 with an independent interval +0.775 to +0.829. Because H10 was the original opposite-direction claim, validation evidence also strengthens rejection of H10. Thus H13 is accepted and closed as a dataset-supported association, while H10 remains rejected and closed. This does not imply causality or biological generality; it means the measured direction is consistent under independent validation in this dataset.

H17 is independently validated. The WRN/MSI-high association, restricted to a comparator population with mutation burden at least 4, was +0.787 in discovery and +0.819 in validation with an independent interval +0.769 to +0.868. This supports the interpretation that the WRN association is not merely an artifact of comparing MSI-high cells against very low-mutation-burden cells. It also indirectly supports H9, but H9 itself is the unrestricted MSI-high effect and has not yet received direct independent validation, so I leave H9 accepted but active as a future validation candidate.

Taken together, the four leading associations are: TP53-wild-type cells have much stronger USP7 dependency (H6, discovery +0.802, not yet independently validated); SMARCA4-loss cells have much stronger SMARCA2 dependency (H7, accepted and independently validated); MSI-high cells have much stronger WRN dependency (H9, accepted with multiple robustness checks and validation of related restricted analysis H17); and KEAP1-loss cells have weaker NFE2L2 dependency/higher dependency score (H13, accepted and independently validated). Each accepted effect is approximately 0.75 to 0.85 on the dependency-score scale, corresponding to roughly two to three outcome standard deviations. Because many dependency scores have negative means, I judged the 10% relative-difference benchmark primarily through effect size and uncertainty rather than as a literal percent change in a negative quantity; these effects clearly exceed scientifically meaningful thresholds within the supplied dataset.

The negative and null findings are now also more interpretable. Same-target dependency claims were not supported: KRAS mutation did not predict KRAS dependency, BRAF V600E did not predict BRAF dependency, EGFR amplification did not predict EGFR dependency after conditional checks, and ERBB2 amplification did not predict ERBB2 dependency. PIK3CA mutation did not predict STAT3 dependency. MYC amplification did not predict POLR2A dependency, and the high-MYC-expression refinement of RPL11 was also null. TP53 loss did not predict MDM2 dependency and did not support a meaningful DHX9 association in the hypothesized direction. MSI-high did not predict KIF18A dependency. KRAS mutation did not show the predicted weaker RIT1 dependency among BRAF-wild-type cells. Interaction tests found no reliable evidence that ARID1A loss modifies the SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 effect, that TP53 loss modifies the KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 effect, that ARID1A loss modifies the USP7/TP53 association, or that TP53 loss modifies the SMARCA4/SMARCA2 association.

The main remaining uncertainty is no longer statistical significance for the leading effects but scientific interpretation and generalization. KEAP1-loss cells having weaker NFE2L2 dependency is consistent and now validated, but its mechanistic meaning is not established by this dataset. Similarly, TP53-wild-type cells having stronger USP7 dependency could reflect selective pressure, scoring artifacts, co-alteration structure, or real biological dependency; the data show an association, not a causal mechanism. Likewise, all conclusions remain limited to the supplied lung cell-line population and measured assays; they should not be described as clinical biomarkers or generalizable causal rules.

The most informative next step is to pursue independent validation for the remaining accepted main effect H6 USP7/TP53-wild-type dependency, and then for H9 WRN/MSI-high if validation capacity remains. Because only one new validation request is available at each appraise cycle, H6 is the higher priority because it is a large accepted main effect lacking direct independent replication. In parallel, I registered non-KY-library refinements of the four leading associations to test whether the effects generalize across the major screen-library context rather than being confined to the KY subset. The active discovery queue should continue to cover unresolved outcomes and predictors, but direct validation of H6 and H9 should take precedence when appropriate.

The highest-value next comparisons are context-robustness tests for the four large accepted associations rather than another broad search for new predictors. The current supported pattern in the supplied lung-cell-line dataset is very strong for TP53 wild-type stronger USP7 dependency (H6), SMARCA4-loss stronger SMARCA2 dependency (H7, independently validated), MSI-high stronger WRN dependency (H9, with robustness checks and validation of the higher-TMB-restricted version H17), and KEAP1-loss weaker NFE2L2 dependency / higher NFE2L2 score (H13, independently validated). All estimates are interpreted under the signed convention: direction -1 means a positive estimate is stronger dependency / more negative score in the exposed group; direction +1 means a positive estimate is weaker dependency / higher score in the exposed group.

I registered four adherent-culture robustness tests. The scientific hypothesis is that if the accepted associations are not merely artifacts of a few non-adherent culture contexts or cell-line screen conditions, they should retain near-full effect size among the large adherent subset. For USP7, TP53 wild-type cells are expected to remain more dependent than TP53-loss cells, so direction -1 with anticipated raw signed positive. For SMARCA2, SMARCA4-loss cells are expected to remain more dependent than SMARCA4-intact cells. For WRN, MSI-high cells are expected to remain more dependent than MSI-low cells. For NFE2L2, KEAP1-loss cells are expected to remain less dependent, i.e. have a higher/less negative score, so direction +1. Plausible alternatives are that an association is driven by non-adherent or low-frequency culture contexts, or that culture mode is correlated with screen quality or a distinct biological subgroup. If the adherent estimate remains around 0.75 to 0.85, that would materially strengthen interpretation as a broad dataset association. If it collapses toward zero, the effect should be interpreted as context-specific and not generalizable across the measured culture settings.

I deferred several currently active lower-priority claims to keep the next analysis focused. H27 and H28 are lower-priority because related mechanistic checks for KIF18A and MYC/RPL11 have already produced small or near-null results. H29 is lower-priority because EGFR amplification direct-target and conditional claims have already been rejected. H32, H34, H35, and H36 test lineage-subtype robustness for effects that are either already independently validated or already supported in adenocarcinoma and other subsets; adenocarcinoma is the majority subset and therefore adds less information than validation or the new culture-context tests. H52 is deferred because high-MYC-expression refinement of POLR2A is closely related to the high-MYC RPL11 test, which was null, while direct MYC-POLR2A was also null.

The next appraise cycle should prioritize independent validation of H6 if a validation request can be paired with the new results. H6 is the only large accepted main effect lacking direct independent validation; H7 and H13 are already validated, and H9 has strong validation-adjacent evidence through H17 but still needs direct independent replication. If H6 validates and validation capacity remains, H9 should be the next validation target. All conclusions remain associations within this dataset and its measured assays, not causal effects, clinical biomarker claims, or externally generalizable mechanisms.

This analysis batch prioritizes (1) technical/context robustness of the four large accepted associations and (2) limited additional outcome/predictor coverage. The four accepted effects are H6 TP53-wild-type stronger USP7 dependency, H7 SMARCA4-loss stronger SMARCA2 dependency, H9 MSI-high stronger WRN dependency, and H13 KEAP1-loss weaker NFE2L2 dependency/higher NFE2L2 score. H54-H57 test these associations in the non-KY CRISPR-library context, which is a distinct screen-technology context from the KY library. H58-H61 test them in the large adherent-culture context, which asks whether the associations are artifacts of a smaller non-adherent or atypical culture group. H26 tests DHX9 with MSI-high status, adding a new predictor-outcome comparison for an outcome where MSI has not yet been assessed. H30 tests MDM2 with MYC amplification among TP53-wild-type cells, a mechanistically motivated check because TP53 status is central to MDM2 biology and MYC amplification may create additional TP53-pathway context. I deliberately do not rerun H6 or H9: they already have strong discovery evidence, and the more informative next action for them is independent validation at the next appraise stage, not repeated cached discovery. I also do not request deferred lineage-subtype or NFE2L2-by-TP53 strata claims in this batch because the current non-KY and adherent-culture robustness tests are higher priority and more likely to clarify whether the leading effects are broad within the dataset or confined to screen/culture contexts. All requested comparisons use the registered signed convention: for direction -1, a positive signed estimate means stronger dependency/more negative score in the exposed group; for direction +1, a positive signed estimate means weaker dependency/less negative or higher score in the exposed group. If H54-H61 remain near the large 0.75-0.85 signed-effect range, that will materially support these as broad dataset associations. If a context-specific estimate collapses toward zero, the corresponding main effect should be interpreted as limited to the contexts where it remains large. These remain associations within the supplied lung-cell-line dataset and measured assays, not causal mechanisms or clinically validated biomarkers.

All estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. For direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means stronger dependency / more negative CRISPR dependency score in the exposed group; for direction +1 claims, a positive signed estimate means weaker dependency / less negative or higher score in the exposed group.

H26 (MSI-high associated with stronger DHX9 dependency) is rejected as unsupported: signed estimate +0.017, 95% interval -0.017 to +0.052. The interval includes zero and the point estimate is tiny relative to the DHX9 standard deviation (~0.18), so it is not scientifically meaningful under the clinical-significance context. H30 (MYC amplification associated with stronger MDM2 dependency among TP53-wild-type cells) is also rejected: signed estimate +0.008, interval -0.023 to +0.040. This is essentially null and provides no support for a TP53-context-dependent MYC/MDM2 association.

The eight context-robustness tests are all strongly supportive of the leading accepted associations. For USP7/TP53-wild-type, H54 in the non-KY library gave +0.811 (0.789 to 0.834) and H58 in adherent culture gave +0.802 (0.780 to 0.824), matching the original H6 estimate of +0.802. For WRN/MSI-high, H55 in the non-KY library gave +0.808 (0.774 to 0.843) and H60 in adherent culture gave +0.813 (0.780 to 0.846), also matching H9. For SMARCA2/SMARCA4-loss, H56 in the non-KY library gave +0.772 (0.750 to 0.794) and H59 in adherent culture gave +0.788 (0.765 to 0.811), consistent with H7. For NFE2L2/KEAP1-loss in the reversed direction, H57 in the non-KY library gave +0.797 (0.774 to 0.820) and H61 in adherent culture gave +0.792 (0.768 to 0.815), consistent with H13. Because all intervals are far from zero and point estimates remain roughly 0.77-0.81, these are not context-specific artifacts among the major measured screen-library and culture settings. They materially strengthen interpretation as broad dataset associations, though not as causal or clinically generalizable effects.

Given these results, H6 remains the highest-priority claim for independent validation: it is a very large accepted main effect, now robust across non-KY library and adherent-culture contexts, but it is the only leading accepted effect without direct independent validation. H9 also remains accepted and active, but H17 is already independently validated and H55/H60 further support WRN/MSI-high, so H6 has higher marginal value now.

All estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. For direction -1 claims, a positive estimate means stronger dependency / more negative CRISPR dependency score in the exposed group; for direction +1 claims, a positive estimate means weaker dependency / less negative or higher dependency score in the exposed group.

H6 is now independently validated and should be accepted and closed. The claim is that TP53-wild-type cells have stronger USP7 dependency than TP53-loss cells, with TP53_loss=0 exposed and TP53_loss=1 comparator. Discovery gave +0.802 with a 95% discovery interval +0.782 to +0.822. Independent validation gave +0.811 with an independent interval +0.782 to +0.841. These are nearly identical, extremely large associations relative to the USP7 dependency-score scale, and the validation interval is far from zero. Combined with the non-KY-library robustness result +0.811 and adherent-culture result +0.802, I conclude this is a very robust association within this dataset. The data do not establish why TP53-wild-type cells show stronger USP7 dependency, nor whether the association is clinically meaningful, causal, or externally generalizable.

With H6 validated, the leading supported associations are now all independently validated either directly or through highly related claims: H6 TP53-wild-type stronger USP7 dependency, H7 SMARCA4-loss stronger SMARCA2 dependency, H13 KEAP1-loss weaker NFE2L2 dependency/higher score, and H17 WRN/MSI-high stronger dependency in the higher-mutation-burden comparator population. H9, the unrestricted WRN/MSI-high association, remains accepted and active because it has not received direct independent validation, although it is strongly supported by discovery, validation of the related H17 claim, and robustness checks in non-KY library and adherent-culture contexts.

The scientific picture is that four measured predictors are associated with exceptionally large differences in specific CRISPR dependency scores: TP53 wild-type status with stronger USP7 dependency; SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency; MSI-high status with stronger WRN dependency; and KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, which is the reversed direction from the initial mechanistic guess. Each accepted effect is roughly 0.78 to 0.82 on the dependency-score scale, corresponding to multiple standard deviations of the outcome distribution. Under the 10% clinical-significance framing, literal percent differences are awkward because dependency scores are often negative, but these effects are far larger than any plausible noise threshold and are clearly scientifically meaningful within this dataset.

The negative findings are also scientifically informative. Same-gene or pathway-target hypotheses were largely unsupported: KRAS mutation did not predict KRAS dependency, BRAF V600E did not predict BRAF dependency, EGFR amplification did not predict EGFR dependency even after conditioning away KRAS/BRAF alterations, ERBB2 amplification did not predict ERBB2 dependency, PIK3CA mutation did not predict STAT3 dependency, MYC amplification did not predict POLR2A dependency, high-MYC-expression refinements did not support RPL11, TP53 loss did not predict MDM2 dependency, MSI-high did not predict DHX9 or KIF18A dependency, KRAS mutation did not show the predicted RIT1 pattern among BRAF-wild-type cells, and ERBB2 amplification did not predict TMED10 dependency. Interaction tests found no reliable evidence that ARID1A loss, TP53 loss, or TP53-loss context modifies the leading SMARCA2 or NFE2L2 associations in a meaningful way.

The main unresolved uncertainty is now interpretation rather than significance. The KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 weaker-dependency direction is counterintuitive but consistent across discovery and validation. The USP7/TP53-wild-type effect could reflect biological selectivity, co-alteration structure, screen scoring behavior, or dataset-specific confounding; this dataset cannot decide. The SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 and MSI-high/WRN associations are more biologically plausible and well supported as dataset associations, but still should not be phrased as causal or clinically validated rules. The remaining statistical uncertainty for leading effects is small; the remaining scientific uncertainty is whether these associations generalize beyond this supplied lung-cell-line dataset or reflect particular assay/screen conditions.

The most informative next validation target remains H9 WRN/MSI-high, if validation capacity allows, because it is the only leading accepted main effect not yet directly validated. I registered additional context-robustness hypotheses focused on screen_batch to test whether the four leading associations are stable across the largest technical batch context or show batch-specific heterogeneity. If the main effect remains near 0.75 to 0.85 within batch_a and interaction estimates remain small, this will further support that the leading associations are not batch artifacts. If batch_a shows attenuation or sign reversal, interpretation should narrow substantially to the contexts in which the effect persists.

The current dataset-supported pattern remains four very large associations: TP53 wild-type cells have stronger USP7 dependency (H6), SMARCA4-loss cells have stronger SMARCA2 dependency (H7), MSI-high cells have stronger WRN dependency (H9, with the higher-mutation-burden version H17 independently validated), and KEAP1-loss cells have weaker NFE2L2 dependency, i.e. a higher/less negative score, which is the reverse of the initial mechanistic expectation (H13). All estimates are signed to the registered direction: for direction -1, a positive estimate means stronger dependency / more negative dependency score in the exposed group; for direction +1, a positive estimate means weaker dependency / less negative or higher dependency score in the exposed group.

The next highest-value discoveries are not another broad set of null direct-target tests, but context-robustness checks that ask whether the leading associations survive under higher screen quality and in biologically/technically important strata. I registered four screen-quality refinements using eligibility screen_roc_auc >= 0.95, roughly a high-quality-screen subset near the median or above. The scientific hypothesis is that if these effects are not screen-quality artifacts, they should remain near the large 0.75-0.85 signed range among higher-quality screens. If an effect collapses toward zero in the high-quality subset, the claim should be interpreted as restricted to lower-quality or heterogeneous screen contexts; if it persists, the dataset association becomes harder to attribute to assay noise.

For USP7/TP53-wild-type, I added aneuploidy strata because TP53 loss is commonly associated with aneuploidy and copy-number instability. The high-aneuploidy and low-aneuploidy refinements test whether the USP7 effect is merely a byproduct of the co-occurrence of TP53 loss and aneuploidy, or whether it remains detectable within relatively homogeneous aneuploidy strata. Persistence in both strata would strengthen the USP7 association within this dataset, while strong attenuation would indicate context specificity.

For WRN/MSI-high, I added a higher-mutation-burden refinement with mutation_burden >= 10. H17 already showed the association remains when the comparator population has mutation burden at least 4, and it independently validated. This stricter test asks whether the MSI-high WRN effect is especially robust among MSI-high-like high-TMB lines rather than being driven by contrast against very low mutation-burden comparator lines. If the effect remains near 0.75-0.85, it further supports H9, for which direct independent validation remains the main next priority.

I also added one focused broad exploration: RB1 loss versus KIF18A dependency. RB1 loss can promote chromosomal instability and mitotic stress, and KIF18A contributes to chromosome congression and mitotic fidelity. The directional hypothesis is that RB1-loss cells show stronger KIF18A dependency (direction -1, positive signed estimate), although the same-gene/pathway target dependencies have generally been null in this dataset. A null result would be useful but less surprising; a large result would identify another biologically plausible dependency predictor.

I deferred the four screen_batch interaction claims H63, H65, H67, and H69 to keep the next analysis batch focused on main-effect persistence across batch_a, screen quality, aneuploidy, mutation burden, and one new predictor. The batch main effects H62, H64, H66, and H68 remain active. Interaction terms are still scientifically meaningful, but the four leading effects have already shown consistent main effects across several contexts and several interaction tests have been null or uninformative; therefore batch interactions can wait unless main-effect attenuation appears. After these results, the next appraise should prioritize independent validation of H9 if validation capacity remains and no validation-conflicting evidence appears.

This batch tests the technical and biological robustness of the four leading accepted associations and adds one mechanistically plausible new predictor-outcome comparison. The four screen_batch_a main-effect claims H62, H64, H66, and H68 ask whether the USP7/TP53-wild-type, SMARCA2/SMARCA4-loss, WRN/MSI-high, and NFE2L2/KEAP1-loss effects remain large in the largest technical batch context. The four screen_roc_auc >= 0.95 claims H70, H71, H72, and H73 ask whether the same effects persist among higher-quality screens, reducing concern that they are driven by noisy or lower-quality CRISPR screens. For USP7, H74 and H75 split the effect by high and low aneuploidy to test whether TP53-loss/aneuploidy co-occurrence explains the association; if both strata remain near the large +0.75 to +0.85 signed range, the association is less likely to be a byproduct of aneuploidy alone. H76 refines the WRN/MSI-high association with a stricter high-mutation-burden context, mutation_burden >= 10, to test whether the effect persists when the comparator population is also relatively high-TMB. H77 tests RB1 loss against KIF18A dependency as a focused biological check: RB1 loss may create mitotic stress, and KIF18A is involved in chromosome congression and mitotic fidelity. All estimates will be interpreted in the registered signed direction: for direction -1, positive means stronger dependency / more negative score in the exposed group; for direction +1, positive means weaker dependency / less negative or higher score in the exposed group. No independent validation is requested here; H9 WRN/MSI-high remains the leading validation target for appraise if current robustness evidence remains consistent.

All estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. For direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means stronger dependency / more negative CRISPR dependency score in the exposed group; for direction +1 claims, a positive signed estimate means weaker dependency / less negative or higher score in the exposed group.

The batch_a robustness results support all four leading accepted associations. H62, USP7 dependency comparing TP53-wild-type with TP53-loss within screen_batch=batch_a, gave +0.789 (95% interval +0.749 to +0.828). This is far from zero and essentially matches the overall H6 discovery estimate. H64, SMARCA2 dependency with SMARCA4 loss in batch_a, gave +0.747 (0.709 to 0.785), slightly lower than the overall H7 estimate but still a very large association and far from zero. H66, WRN dependency with MSI-high in batch_a, gave +0.824 (0.766 to 0.882) despite only 37 MSI-high cells in batch_a; the interval is wide but very large and excludes zero. H68, NFE2L2 dependency with KEAP1 loss in batch_a in the reversed direction, gave +0.812 (0.765 to 0.858), indicating weaker NFE2L2 dependency / higher score in KEAP1-loss cells and supporting H13.

The high-screen-quality subset, defined by screen_roc_auc >= 0.95, also supports the same four effects. H70 USP7/TP53-wild-type was +0.804 (0.780 to 0.828). H71 SMARCA2/SMARCA4-loss was +0.790 (0.765 to 0.816). H72 WRN/MSI-high was +0.795 (0.758 to 0.832). H73 NFE2L2/KEAP1-loss was +0.790 (0.763 to 0.816). These estimates are not attenuated toward zero and are consistent with the leading overall effects, making it less plausible that these are artifacts of low screen quality or noisy screens. Multiplicity remains a consideration for context tests, but the consistency across independent technical contexts and the magnitude relative to the dependency-score standard deviations are compelling within this dataset.

The USP7 aneuploidy-strata results further reduce concern that the TP53-wild-type/USP7 association is merely a byproduct of co-occurring aneuploidy. In high aneuploidy, H74 gave +0.801 (0.758 to 0.844); in low aneuploidy, H75 gave +0.816 (0.785 to 0.846). These intervals overlap and remain very large. H76 also strengthens WRN/MSI-high: in the stricter mutation_burden >= 10 stratum, the signed estimate was +0.768 (0.721 to 0.815), still extremely large, even when the comparator population is itself relatively high-mutation-burden. This supports H9 without establishing causality or external generalizability.

The one focused new broad hypothesis, H77 RB1 loss versus KIF18A dependency, is rejected: signed estimate +0.008 (interval -0.019 to +0.036). This is null and not scientifically meaningful given the KIF18A dependency-score scale. Like many other targeted same-gene or pathway-target hypotheses tested so far, it does not show a large measured predictor effect.

Given the new robustness evidence, I request independent validation of H9, the unrestricted WRN/MSI-high association. H9 is now supported by discovery, non-KY library robustness, adherent-culture robustness, batch_a, high screen quality, high mutation burden, and validation of the related H17 restricted claim, but it remains the only leading accepted main effect without direct independent validation. If validation confirms, H9 can be closed as a robust within-dataset association; if validation attenuates, the WRN claim should be narrowed to the specific contexts where it remains large. These findings remain associations within this supplied lung-cell-line dataset, not causal mechanisms or clinically validated biomarker claims.

All estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. For direction -1 claims, a positive estimate means stronger dependency, that is a more negative CRISPR dependency score in the exposed group relative to comparator; for direction +1 claims, a positive estimate means weaker dependency, that is a higher or less negative score in the exposed group.

Due evidence assessment. H9, the unrestricted WRN dependency comparison MSI-high versus not MSI-high, received independent validation R63: signed estimate +0.7896 with independent interval +0.7364 to +0.8429. Discovery R9 was +0.7899, interval +0.7604 to +0.8193. These are nearly identical and extremely large relative to the WRN dependency-score distribution, whose standard deviation is about 0.263. The validation interval remains far from zero even with the validation alpha accounting for multiple validation comparisons. I therefore accept H9 and close its investigation. The within-dataset claim is that MSI-high cells have stronger WRN dependency than non-MSI-high cells.

H17, WRN dependency among mutation_burden >= 4, had validation deadline R39. Validation gave +0.8187, independent interval +0.7695 to +0.8680, closely aligned with discovery R17 +0.7869, interval +0.7567 to +0.8171. This confirms the high-mutation-burden-restricted WRN/MSI-high association and supports, but does not replace, H9 as the main WRN finding. H17 remains accepted and closed.

H13, the reversed NFE2L2/KEAP1-loss claim, had validation deadline R38. Validation gave +0.8020, independent interval +0.7746 to +0.8294, while discovery R10 gave signed +0.7961, interval +0.7759 to +0.8163. Because direction +1 was registered to capture the reverse of the original mechanistic guess, a positive estimate means KEAP1-loss cells have weaker NFE2L2 dependency, i.e. higher or less negative dependency scores, than KEAP1-intact cells. This direction is counterintuitive but stable across discovery and validation and across several context checks. I accept H13 and close it.

Synthesis of the current evidence: the strongest supported findings are four large measured predictor-outcome associations, now all directly independently validated within the supplied dataset or through the corresponding validated main claim. TP53-wild-type status is associated with stronger USP7 dependency (H6, validation R50 +0.811). SMARCA4 loss is associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency (H7, validation R13 +0.805). MSI-high status is associated with stronger WRN dependency (H9, validation R63 +0.790; H17 also validated +0.819 in the mutation_burden >= 4 population). KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, or higher NFE2L2 dependency score, than KEAP1-intact cells (H13, validation R38 +0.802; H10 in the opposite direction is rejected because the raw contrast points the other way).

These effects are scientifically meaningful within this dataset. The leading signed differences are roughly 0.75 to 0.82 dependency-score units, which is more than two standard deviations of the relevant dependency-score distributions and very far from zero. Interpreting them literally as percentages is awkward because dependency scores are often negative, but they are plainly larger than any plausible 10 percent clinical-significance threshold if judged on the outcome scale. The supporting context evidence is also unusually consistent: the four leading associations remain large in non-KY and KY CRISPR libraries, adherent culture, the largest screen batch, high screen-quality screens, different mutation-burden contexts, and both high- and low-aneuploidy strata for USP7.

The negative findings are an important part of the report. Direct same-gene or pathway-target hypotheses are broadly unsupported in this dataset: KRAS mutation did not predict KRAS dependency; BRAF V600E did not predict BRAF dependency; EGFR amplification did not predict EGFR dependency, including among KRAS/BRAF wild-type cells; ERBB2 amplification did not predict ERBB2 dependency; PIK3CA mutation did not predict STAT3 dependency; MYC amplification did not predict POLR2A dependency; high MYC expression did not support RPL11; TP53 loss did not predict MDM2 dependency; MSI-high did not predict DHX9 or KIF18A dependency; KRAS mutation did not show the predicted RIT1 pattern among BRAF wild-type cells; ERBB2 amplification did not predict TMED10 dependency; and RB1 loss did not predict KIF18A dependency. Interaction tests so far have not shown meaningful modification of the leading SMARCA2 or NFE2L2 associations by ARID1A loss or TP53-loss status. Formal batch and lineage interactions remain registered but unresolved; however, the main effects are already robust within batch_a, adenocarcinoma, library, culture, screen-quality, and mutation-burden contexts, and the direct validation of H9 closes the most important remaining gap.

Unresolved uncertainty is now primarily interpretive and external, not statistical. These are associations within the supplied lung-cell-line-like dataset. They do not establish causality, mechanistic synthetic lethality, drug response, or clinical biomarker behavior. The KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 weaker-dependency direction is especially biologically counterintuitive and may reflect dataset-specific structure, co-alteration patterns, scoring behavior, or some unmeasured confounder. Likewise, USP7/TP53-wild-type could reflect genuine biology or co-occurring genomic/assay structure; the aneuploidy-strata results reduce one specific confounding concern but do not prove mechanism. Generalizability outside this dataset, lineage, screen library, culture setting, and batch structure remains untested.

Most informative next analysis: because all leading main effects are validated, the next high-value work is to (1) formally test major technical modifiers of the validated effects, starting with library-specific heterogeneity as registered in the current proposal batch, and (2) probe additional biologically plausible predictor-outcome pairs, especially DNA-repair/mitotic-stress hypotheses such as BRCA2 loss for WRN, DHX9, KIF18A, and POLR2A, plus STK11 loss for KRAS dependency. If a new context or predictor estimate approaches the magnitude of the leading validated effects and is not already explained by the accepted associations, it would merit validation; otherwise, the current within-dataset conclusion is four robust dependency-score associations and a broad null result for many direct-target dependency predictions.

All estimates will be interpreted in the registered signed direction. For direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means stronger dependency, that is a more negative CRISPR dependency score in the exposed group relative to comparator. For direction +1 claims, such as the NFE2L2/KEAP1-loss refinement, a positive signed estimate means weaker dependency or a higher, less negative dependency score in KEAP1-loss cells. The current accepted main effects are unusually large within this dataset, roughly +0.78 to +0.82 signed dependency-score units, so future results should be judged against that scale: null direct-target estimates have generally been within a few hundredths of a unit, whereas a candidate new association should approach at least the lower hundreds, and ideally the 0.75 to 0.85 range, to be considered a major new finding. Modest estimates with intervals excluding zero should still be interpreted cautiously because many context and predictor hypotheses create multiplicity. In this explore stage I defer the four library-interaction tests H78 through H81 and one lower-priority BRCA2/KIF18A test H84 so that the next analysis batch can prioritize two scientific goals: testing whether the four leading validated associations persist inside specific co-alteration contexts, and probing new biologically motivated predictor-outcome pairs beyond direct same-gene dependency predictions. The four co-alteration refinements test whether the large USP7/TP53-wild-type, SMARCA2/SMARCA4-loss, WRN/MSI-high, and reversed NFE2L2/KEAP1-loss effects remain large when restricted to KEAP1-loss, STK11-loss, TP53-loss, and STK11-loss cell lines respectively. If they persist near the leading effect magnitude, the associations become less plausibly carried by a single co-occurring alteration context. If they attenuate, the claims should be narrowed to co-alteration-free or specific genomic contexts. The four new broad predictor hypotheses are STK11 loss with POLR2A dependency, STK11 loss with RPL11 dependency, CDKN2A loss with POLR2A dependency, and PTEN loss with STAT3 dependency. These are direction -1 hypotheses in which loss of the predictor is expected to make cells more dependent on the outcome gene, but they are not same-gene or same-pathway target tests and therefore require more cautious interpretation if positive. No validation is requested in this explore stage; validation will be considered only after appraising these context-specific persistence and new predictor results.

This analysis batch tests the highest-value unresolved comparisons registered after the leading main effects have been accepted and validated. The first group tests whether the four large validated associations persist inside important co-alteration contexts: USP7/TP53-wild-type within KEAP1-loss cells, SMARCA2/SMARCA4-loss within STK11-loss cells, WRN/MSI-high within TP53-loss cells, and NFE2L2/KEAP1-loss in the reversed direction within STK11-loss cells. These are falsifiable independence checks: persistence near the current +0.75 to +0.85 signed range would reduce concern that the main association is carried entirely by that co-alteration context, while attenuation would require narrowing the main claim to co-alteration-specific settings. The second group tests new biologically motivated predictor-outcome pairs. BRCA2 loss is examined against WRN, DHX9, and POLR2A dependency because BRCA2 loss may create DNA-repair and replication-stress vulnerabilities; BRCA2/KIF18A remains deferred for now. STK11 loss is tested against KRAS, POLR2A, and RPL11 dependency because STK11/LKB1 loss can alter metabolic stress and biosynthetic signaling. CDKN2A loss is tested against POLR2A dependency and PTEN loss against STAT3 dependency as additional plausible checkpoint/signaling hypotheses. All returned estimates will be interpreted as already signed to the registered hypothesis direction: for direction -1, positive means stronger dependency or a more negative dependency score in the exposed group; for direction +1, positive means weaker dependency or a higher, less negative score in the exposed group. No validation is requested at this stage; validation will be considered only after appraising whether any new effect is large enough to be scientifically meaningful and not merely another context duplication.

All new estimates are already signed to the registered direction. For direction -1 claims, a positive estimate means stronger dependency, i.e. a more negative CRISPR dependency score in the exposed group; for direction +1 claims, a positive estimate means weaker dependency or a higher dependency score in the exposed group. The BRCA2-loss hypotheses are null across the DNA-repair/replication-stress genes tested here: H82 WRN, estimate +0.00007 with interval -0.045 to +0.045; H83 DHX9, +0.012 with interval -0.020 to +0.044; and H85 POLR2A, +0.013 with interval -0.019 to +0.046. These are within the usual null band and do not support strong biological effects despite mechanistic plausibility. I reject and close them. Likewise, the STK11-loss broad predictors are null for KRAS dependency, H86 estimate -0.002 with interval -0.022 to +0.018; for POLR2A dependency, H91 estimate +0.011 with interval -0.008 to +0.031; and for RPL11 dependency, H92 estimate -0.012 with interval -0.033 to +0.009. The CDKN2A-loss hypothesis against POLR2A is also null, H93 estimate +0.002 with interval -0.018 to +0.022. All are rejected and closed. These results extend the broader pattern that most direct or plausible gene-alteration dependency predictions in this dataset are small or absent, whereas a small set of very large associations dominate the dependency landscape.

The co-alteration persistence tests support the leading accepted effects. H87, USP7 dependency among TP53-wild-type versus TP53-loss cells restricted to KEAP1-loss cells, gave +0.794 with interval +0.754 to +0.834, essentially matching the overall USP7/TP53-wild-type effect. H88, SMARCA2 dependency among SMARCA4-loss versus intact cells restricted to STK11-loss cells, gave +0.769 with interval +0.727 to +0.811, also close to the overall SMARCA2/SMARCA4-loss effect. H89, WRN dependency among MSI-high versus non-MSI-high cells restricted to TP53-loss cells, gave +0.833 with interval +0.765 to +0.900. The MSI-high/TP53-loss cell is small, with only 24 exposed observations, so the interval is wide, but the effect remains far from zero. H90, the reversed NFE2L2/KEAP1-loss effect restricted to STK11-loss cells, gave +0.775 with interval +0.727 to +0.823, again supporting the counterintuitive direction that KEAP1-loss cells have weaker NFE2L2 dependency. These context checks make it less plausible that the leading associations are carried entirely by one co-occurring alteration context, but they remain within-dataset associations, not causal claims. I accept and close H87-H90.

The one genuinely new positive finding is H94: PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency, signed estimate +0.267 with interval +0.215 to +0.319, in 266 versus 1734 cell lines. This is not in the huge +0.75 to +0.85 range of the leading four effects, but it is still substantial on the dependency-score scale: the STAT3 dependency-score standard deviation is about 0.246, so this difference is roughly one standard deviation and is far beyond the null band seen in other predictor tests. The interval excludes zero and the sample sizes are adequate. Given the large number of comparisons tested, however, I cannot yet regard it as equally secure as the validated main effects. Its magnitude is scientifically meaningful, but its status should be tested independently. Therefore I accept H94 as a promising within-dataset association, keep its investigation active, and request independent validation of H94.

The main alternative explanations for H94 are residual confounding by correlated genomic or expression features, multiplicity across many null predictor-outcome tests, and dataset-specific biological structure. PTEN loss may co-occur with pathways that alter STAT3 dependency, or it may reflect a broader PTEN/PI3K/mTOR/STAT signaling axis. These findings remain associations measured in the supplied lung-cell-line-like dataset; they do not establish causality, drug sensitivity, or external clinical generalizability. I have registered follow-up tests for PTEN/STAT3 robustness and modification, including interaction by TP53 loss, persistence in high-quality screens, and persistence in KRAS-wild-type and non-KY-library contexts.

All estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. For direction -1 claims, a positive estimate means stronger dependency, i.e. a more negative CRISPR dependency score in the exposed group relative to comparator. For direction +1 claims, a positive estimate means weaker dependency or a higher, less negative dependency score in the exposed group.  Due assessment H6: TP53-wild-type versus TP53-loss status associated with stronger USP7 dependency received independent validation R50: signed estimate +0.8115 with independent interval +0.7821 to +0.8408 at the validation-adjusted level. This matches discovery R6 +0.8019 and is far beyond the small null band seen in rejected predictor tests. H6 is accepted and closed as a robust within-dataset association.  Due assessment H94: PTEN loss versus PTEN-intact status associated with stronger STAT3 dependency received independent validation R76: signed estimate +0.2919 with independent interval +0.2135 to +0.3704. This is concordant with discovery R75 +0.2674, interval +0.2153 to +0.3195. The validation interval excludes zero even with the stricter independent interval. The effect is smaller than the leading four associations but is still scientifically meaningful on the dependency-score scale: dependency_STAT3 has SD about 0.246, so the effect is roughly 1.2 SD, and the lower confidence bound is roughly 0.9 SD. Thus I accept H94 as a newly supported within-dataset association but keep its investigation active pending robustness and specificity checks.  Due assessment H16: the ARID1A-loss interaction in the SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 dependency comparison received independent validation R77: signed estimate +0.0162 with interval -0.0543 to +0.0868. Discovery R16 was +0.0373 with interval -0.0148 to +0.0894. Both are small and compatible with no meaningful modification, especially relative to the huge main SMARCA4-loss effect around +0.78 to +0.81. I reject H16 and close it. This supports interpreting H7 as a broad SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 association not materially modified by ARID1A loss in this dataset.  Synthesis of supported findings: the strongest within-dataset predictor-outcome associations are now (1) TP53-wild-type status with stronger USP7 dependency, (2) SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, (3) MSI-high status with stronger WRN dependency, including the mutation_burden >= 4 restriction, and (4) KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, meaning higher or less negative NFE2L2 dependency scores than KEAP1-intact cells. These four are independently validated and remain large across libraries, culture, batch_a, high screen quality, mutation-burden contexts, aneuploidy strata for USP7, and several co-alteration restrictions. The new fifth supported association is PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency, discovery and validation estimates near +0.27 to +0.29. This is smaller than the leading four but well above the usual null band and above plausible clinical-scale thresholds if dependency-score units are interpreted directly.  Negative findings are substantial: direct same-gene or pathway-target dependency predictions were broadly null, including KRAS mutation/KRAS, BRAF V600E/BRAF, EGFR amplification/EGFR even among KRAS/BRAF wild-type contexts, ERBB2 amplification/ERBB2, PIK3CA/STAT3, MYC/POLR2A, high MYC/RPL11, TP53 loss/MDM2, MSI-high/DHX9, MSI-high/KIF18A, KRAS/RIT1, ERBB2/TMED10, RB1/KIF18A, MYC/MDM2 among TP53-WT, BRCA2 loss with WRN/DHX9/POLR2A, STK11 loss with KRAS/POLR2A/RPL11, and CDKN2A loss with POLR2A. Interaction tests have not shown meaningful modification of the leading associations by ARID1A loss or TP53-loss status, and ARID1A modification of SMARCA2/SMARCA4-loss is now independently null.  Unresolved uncertainty is mainly interpretive and external. The accepted effects are measured associations within this supplied lung-cell-line-like dataset. They do not prove causality, mechanistic synthetic lethality, drug response, or clinical biomarker behavior. The KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 weaker-dependency direction remains biologically counterintuitive and could reflect dataset-specific structure, co-alteration patterns, scoring behavior, or confounding. USP7/TP53-wild-type and PTEN/STAT3 could also reflect correlated genomic or pathway features. The most informative next analysis is to complete the PTEN/STAT3 robustness battery: interaction by TP53 loss, high-quality screens, KRAS wild-type, non-KY library, batch_a, adherent culture, adenocarcinoma subtype, and MYC-amplification interaction, plus one specificity check using PTEN loss against KRAS dependency. If PTEN/STAT3 persists across these contexts, it should be closed as a fifth robust within-dataset association; if it attenuates in key subsets, the claim should be narrowed to the context in which it remains large. Formal library, batch, and lineage interaction tests for the leading four effects remain secondary because their main effects are already robust in those subset analyses.
